newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian exchanges open for trade on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Indian exchanges open for trade on Saturday.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange said on Friday it will be open for trading on Saturday from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0430-0830 GMT).
The Bombay and Calcutta exchanges said on Thursday they will stay open on Saturday due to unfolding political events.
The Bombay Stock Exchange will open from 10 a.m. to 1.30 p.m. and Calcutta will be open from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. (0430-0830 GMT).
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's minority coalition faces defeat in parliament on Friday after its mainstay ally and the largest opposition party both decided to vote against them.
Analysts believe the political impasse could lead to snap polls.
Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India have asked all exchanges to stay open on Saturday to give investors an opportunity to trade as political developments unfold.
